THE LOAD ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS THE WHOLE FILM. Original single continuous rod: design load at each connection 20.3 kips. As built with two interrupted rods: 40.7 kips at the fourth-floor connection - essentially doubled, NBS's own word, Conclusion 6. Code-expected ultimate capacity at 40.7 kips design load with the AISC factor of safety of 1.67: at least 68 kips. Actual average ultimate capacity of the six fourth-floor connections: 18.6 kips. Load actually on the most heavily loaded connection on the night: 21.4 kips = 31 percent of the 68 kips the code expected, and 53 percent of the 40.7 kips design load. Had the change never been made: required ultimate 1.67 x 20.3 = 33.9 kips against an available 20.5 kips, i.e. about 60 percent - still illegal, but it would have held that night (NBS Conclusion 8). Source: NBS BSS 143 sections 10.2, 10.3, 10.5 and chapter 11.

THE NUMBER TRAP. NBS's 31 percent is a LOAD ratio (21.4 / 68), not a CAPACITY ratio. The as-built capacity ratio is 18.6 / 68 = about 27 percent and is OUR arithmetic - NBS never states it. The Missouri Court of Appeals conflates the two in its own footnote 12, so that footnote must never be quoted for the engineering. Ledger forbidden claim 1.

DEATH TOLL. Use 114, citing Duncan v. Missouri Bd., 744 S.W.2d 524 (Mo. App. 1988). NBS BSS 143 (May 1982) says 111 killed plus two of the injured who subsequently died = 113. No retrieved document explains the difference and the film must not invent one. Injured: 'at least 186' (court) or 188 (NBS). NOT 216 - that figure appears in no retrieved source. Ledger forbidden claims 3 and 4.

RIGHTS - CATEGORY 1. NO third-party broadcast or news footage or photographs of any kind. Not the KMBC TV videotape, not the Kansas City Star or Kansas City Times photographs, not rescue footage, not blurred, not behind a graphic. This is the most tempting case on the whole slate for a violation. Ledger forbidden claim 10.

DEPICTION - DECIDED, NOT LEFT TO THE DESIGNER. No body, no injured person, no rescue, no debris with a person under it, and no depiction of the crowded lobby at or near the moment of collapse from any angle. The film shows the empty ballroom, the atrium filling at 3 p.m., the rod, the box beam assembling itself in 3D, the two drawings side by side, the load bar, the rod-and-washer pull-through, and NBS's own rescue timeline as type on black. Every prohibited image has a named replacement in ledger section 12.

NO VICTIM IS NAMED AND NO REAL LIKENESS APPEARS. Neither NBS nor the court names a victim. The named people in this film are the ones the record names for documented professional acts: Duncan, Gillum, Havens Steel Company, Mayor Berkley, Judge Deutsch, Judge Smith. Engineers appear as hands, a seal and an empty stool - never a face.

R3 CONSTRAINTS ON THE ENGINEERS. Daniel M. Duncan and Jack D. Gillum may be living. Every criticism must be a quoted finding of the Missouri Administrative Hearing Commission as reproduced in 744 S.W.2d 524, or an NBS conclusion. No claim about knowledge, intent, motive, character or finances beyond them. They were NEVER criminally charged - the ending is the first American licence revocation for gross negligence, in January 1986, affirmed on appeal in January 1988.

DO NOT STAGE THE TELEPHONE CALL. The engineering-ethics teaching version (Havens rings G.C.E., someone approves, G.C.E. denies the call) is in neither the federal report nor the appellate opinion. What the record does establish is better: the drawings told the fabricator the engineer had designed the connection while the engineer intended the fabricator to design it, and a technician who queried the change was told it was 'basically the same as the one rod concept'. Ledger forbidden claim 5.

NOVELTY. Same family as EP60 surfside (building collapse, mass casualty, federal forensic investigation). Judged NOT too close - different cause (one decision vs forty years of decay), different epistemics (exact arithmetic vs contested margins) and the opposite ending (licences revoked vs no accountability).
